What is a motherboard?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answerThe connections that matterCompatibility comes firstWhen you need the manualFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the processor, memory, storage, and other components. Its connections determine which parts can work together.

The connections that matter

A motherboard provides a CPU socket, memory slots, storage connections, and expansion slots. It also connects the case’s buttons and ports. The manual explains the location and limits of each connector.

Compatibility comes first

A matching CPU socket is necessary but may not be enough: firmware and chipset support matter too. Check the board manufacturer’s CPU support list and memory specifications. Case size and mounting points also need to match.

When you need the manual

Use the manual for memory slot order, front-panel wiring, and storage installation. Never force a connector. Turn off and unplug the computer before working inside it.

What is RAM?

RAM is your computer’s short-term working memory. It holds the information your apps are using right now. Storage keeps your files when the power is off; RAM does not.
